terms.definition: A chemical bond formed when two atoms share a pair of electrons.
terms.function: Holds the atoms of a molecule together — both nuclei pull on the shared pair.
terms.whereItIs: The band between the oxygen and hydrogen atoms in the water molecule.
terms.whyItMatters: Covalent bonds build water, air, and nearly every molecule in living things.

terms.definition: A pair of electrons that two atoms both pull on and both effectively own.
terms.function: Lets each atom feel closer to a full outer shell without either stealing an electron.
terms.whereItIs: The two small teal dots between the atoms in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the actual 'stuff' of a covalent bond.

terms.definition: Two or more atoms held together by covalent bonds.
terms.function: The smallest unit of a covalent compound that still has its properties.
terms.whereItIs: The whole water molecule in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Molecules are what covalent bonds build — the fundamental particles of most familiar substances.

terms.definition: A covalent bond in which two pairs of electrons are shared between the same two atoms.
terms.function: Holds atoms even more tightly — found in O₂, CO₂, and many important molecules.
terms.whereItIs: Shown as two parallel rods in the oxygen molecule layer.
terms.whyItMatters: Double bonds store energy and shape molecules like carbon dioxide.
